title: Your laptop delivery needs $2.40
scenario: You are waiting for a new laptop when a text says the courier needs a $2.40 redelivery fee before 3 p.m. The message includes a tracking number that looks similar to your real one.

answers.A: Check the order and tracking in the retailer/carrier app or website you open yourself.
answers.B: Contact the carrier independently if the tracking status is unclear.
answers.C: Pay the small fee because the delivery timing and tracking number are close enough.

explanation: Expected high-value packages make delivery phishing particularly believable. Tiny fees can be bait for card and identity data.
proTip: Expected package, unexpected payment path: verify.
